questions.question: An invented aircraft has its CG at xcg = 310 in, aft of the datum. The leading edge of c̄ is at xLEMAC = 280 in, and c̄ = 100 in. What is x̄cg?
questions.explanation: x̄cg = (xcg − xLEMAC)/c̄ = (310 − 280)/100 = 0.30. Dividing the position from the datum by c̄ gives 3.10, which is not a position on the chord.

questions.question: On the CG envelope of the Cirrus SR22 the forward limit moves aft as the weight rises, and the aft limit is one vertical line. Why does the aft limit stay at the same position at every weight?
options: The static margin does not depend on the weight
The nose landing gear limit does not depend on the weight
The elevator limit at rotation does not depend on the weight
The fuel burn does not move the CG of the aircraft
questions.explanation: The aft limit comes from the minimum static margin, and the static margin does not depend on the weight. The nose landing gear and the elevator at takeoff rotation are the causes of the sloped forward limit.

questions.question: The CG of a stable aircraft moves aft. What happens to the line of CM,cg against CL?
options: It flattens, and it is horizontal with the CG at the neutral point
It steepens, and it falls fastest with the CG at the neutral point
It shifts down at the same slope, and the trim CL falls
It flattens, and it is horizontal with the CG at the wing aerodynamic center
questions.explanation: The slope of the line is −SM, with SM = x̄n − x̄cg, so moving the CG aft flattens it until it is horizontal at the neutral point. The tail places the neutral point aft of the wing aerodynamic center.

questions.question: On the scissor plot, the cut is moved up to a larger tail area ratio St/S. What happens to the CG limits?
options: The forward limit moves forward, and the aft limit moves aft
The forward limit stays, and the aft limit moves aft
The forward limit moves aft, and the aft limit moves aft
The forward limit moves aft, and the aft limit moves forward
questions.explanation: The feasible region is above every line. The control lines on its left fall to the right and the stability and stall-recovery lines on its right rise, so a higher cut is longer at both ends.

questions.question: In the trim diagram, the line of δe,trim for the forward CG meets the elevator limit at a high CL,trim. What does that point give?
options: The slowest speed the aircraft can trim at that CG
The fastest speed the aircraft can trim at that CG
The stall speed of the wing at that CG
The speed at which the static margin reaches zero
questions.explanation: The forward CG needs the largest elevator deflection, trailing edge up, at high lift, and a high CL = W/(qS) means a low speed. Beyond the elevator limit the moment about the CG cannot be brought to zero, so the aircraft cannot trim at a lower speed.

questions.question: Why is the trim drag largest at the forward CG?
options: The tail download is largest, and the wing must lift more than the weight
The tail upload is largest, and the wing lifts less than the weight
The trim angle of attack is largest, and CD0 rises with it
The static margin is smallest, and the elevator must deflect more
questions.explanation: A download on the tail makes the wing lift more than the weight: the induced drag of the wing rises, and the tail adds its own. The forward CG has the largest static margin and needs the largest elevator deflection, trailing edge up, to trim.

questions.question: High-wing swept transports are built with anhedral. Why?
options: Sweep and the high wing give too much dihedral effect, and anhedral removes some
Sweep and the high wing make Cℓβ positive, and anhedral makes it negative
Sweep and the high wing reduce the yaw stiffness Cnβ, and anhedral restores it
Sweep and the high wing reduce the roll damping Cℓp, and anhedral restores it
questions.explanation: Sweep and a high wing each add a negative part to Cℓβ, and too much dihedral effect is a handling problem. A negative dihedral angle adds a positive part and brings Cℓβ back into range.

questions.section: Step 5: the engine-out case and the rudder
questions.question: In the engine-out case, the rotation speed must lie above the minimum control speed Vmc. What fails below Vmc?
options: The rudder at its largest deflection cannot balance the yawing moment of the engines
The wing at its largest lift coefficient cannot carry the weight of the aircraft
The elevator at its largest deflection cannot rotate the aircraft about the main gear
The live engine at its largest thrust cannot balance the drag of the aircraft
questions.explanation: The rudder moment q S b |Cnδr| δr,max is proportional to q. Vmc is the speed at which it just balances the yawing moment (T + Ddead) ye of the live and the failed engine; below that speed the rudder moment is too small.
